newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says EU failed to implement fruit deal.
newsitem.headline: Poland says EU failed to implement fruit deal.

text.p: Poland's foreign ministry complained in a note to the European Commission on Friday that the EU had failed to carry out an agreement easing exports of Polish soft fruit, it said in a statement.

The note to envoys from the Netherlands and European Commission in Warsaw, said that one month after the EU-Poland Association council met in Luxembourg, several agreements reached then or before had not been implemented.
"Regret was expressed that the EU had decided to retain for 1996/97 the minimum price regime for imports of soft fruits for the coming production season," the statement said.
"This means that an agreement concerning a reduction of prices and tariffs concluded on 21 January 1997 will not come into force as the Polish side had expected," it said.
This delay, plus a lack of annual increases in preferential quotas and new quota regulations, would mean major losses for Polish exporters, it said.
"Such unfavourable trade conditions will deepen Poland's agriculture trade deficit."
The fruit row is one of several trade issues complicating Poland's ties with the EU. Warsaw has an association agreement with the EU, which it plans to join by around 2002.
Poland is concerned over a farm trade deficit with the EU which rose last year to $1 billion from $476 million in 1995.
The ministry recalled that Poland this year agreed to cut VAT charges on citrus fruit as a goodwill gesture -- a move prompted by demands from EU member Spain.
It also said the EU had withdrawn preferences for the export of young cattle.
